text: Three months ago, Everpeak's first churn model scored an offline AUC of 0.98 -- a number that looked almost too good to be true.
Two features, logins_last_30d and days_since_last_login, were anchored to each account's own churn date instead of a fixed observation date.
SHAP had already flagged those two features as dominating nearly every prediction -- the tell, in hindsight, that something was wrong.
A time-consistent backtest put the real original number at 0.74. After the fix, the corrected model lands at an honest AUC of 0.79.
Nobody's renewal decisions were ever made against 0.98 -- the gap was caught in validation. Next: turning this trusted score into Tom's weekly workflow.
